# CityMETER · Commercial District

> The central neighbourhood registry of CityMETER (release 2026-11-17: 358 closed draft outlines, plus 37 lodging areas of its lodging screen counted as neighbourhoods here by the owner's decision of 2026-11-18; 395 outlines in 77 provinces, 95.0 km²) against the located records of 16 CityMETER demo datasets — Land (hotels, industrial estates, offices, shopping centers), Location (camera shops, factories, fitness, grocery, luxury brands, pharmacies, restaurants), Living (government offices, hospitals, schools, rail stations, universities): what each neighbourhood stands out for against named peers, which datasets rise together across neighbourhoods, which neighbourhoods have a similar mix, and up to four side by side. A Landometer CityMETER demo, release 0.2.0 (2026-11-18), Thai with an English reading (?lang=en). Registry read 2026-11-18; each dataset's date is its own.

What one figure means:
- neighbourhood = a closed draft outline of the central registry (code CMN-TH-…). Drafts pending local confirmation: not an administrative boundary, a legal line or a title. 27 more registry codes have no closed outline yet; they are searchable, never counted.
- count = a dataset's records with a point inside the outline, in the dataset's own unit (places, branches, stores, points of sale, registrations, records, station-line records). Counts of two datasets are never added.
- per km² = count ÷ the registry's own area for the neighbourhood.
- no data (—) = the dataset has no located record in the neighbourhood's province: unknown, never 0. 0 = the dataset reaches the province, nothing of it lies inside the outline.
- share = a dataset's records inside the neighbourhoods ÷ its located records (nationwide or in the province).
- highlight = near the top among named peers: ≥ 5% of the dataset's located records nationwide, a count or density rank in the top quarter (with the number of peers), or one of the few neighbourhoods holding any.
- comes together = Spearman's ρ of density across the neighbourhoods both datasets cover (a correlation, not a cause).
- similar mix = correlation of centred log density across the datasets two neighbourhoods share (an inference, a starting point for a comparison).

Snapshot (release 0.1.0; fixtures, recompute from data):
- 395 neighbourhoods = 0.018% of the area of the 77 provinces, but 69% of the located luxury points of sale (237 of 345), 42% of the offices (179 of 427), 40% of the camera shops (94 of 236), 38% of the fitness branches (56 of 149), 29% of the rail station-line records (88 of 301); 0 of 69 industrial estates.
- Lodging screen of the registry (0.2.0): 268 proposals from 30,730 lodging records, walking 400/800 m; 193 supported, 75 held; shown per neighbourhood as a walking model, not a survey.
- Bangkok: 75 neighbourhoods = 1.3% of the province; 82% of its luxury points of sale (232 of 284).
- Strongest pairs: camera shops + luxury brands ρ 0.67 (136 neighbourhoods), fitness + luxury brands 0.56, camera shops + fitness 0.54, offices + fitness 0.52, grocery + restaurants 0.40.

Deep links (https://montri-th.github.io/commercialdistrict/):
- ?at={province code} — e.g. BKK, CMI, PKT (production codes)
- ?f.neighborhood={CMN-TH code} — a neighbourhood (with its province in at)
- ?m={dataset} — colour by one dataset's density: hotel, industrialestate, office, shoppingcenter, camera, factory, fitness, grocery, luxurybrands, pharmacy, restaurant, governmentoffice, hospital, school, transit, university
- Rail context of the map (0.2.3): urban rail lines in service (solid) and under construction (dashed), stations, interchanges and the national rail stops with scheduled trips, from CityMETER Transit (data/rail.json; the stations are the file the dataset สถานีราง counts) — drawn in one neutral ink under the neighbourhoods, never counted. Choosing a neighbourhood fits the map to its outline.
- 0.2.4: the rail is drawn in a darker neutral ink and wider (still under the outlines); the outline of นิมมาน–เมญ่า (CMN-TH-FB55C19EF1, Chiang Mai) is extended across Huay Kaew Road to take in Maya, Kad Rin Kham, The Wall and Chiang Mai Polytechnic College, on the owner's word of 18 Nov 2026, drawn by the registry's outline rules from the registry outline and OpenStreetMap ways (amendments/; rows[].amended, meta.amendments) — awaiting the registry's next release
- 0.2.5: a neighbourhood's area reads in rai (ไร่; 1 rai = 1,600 m²) instead of hectares — list, card, comparison, table and provenance — with its km² in the area tile's hover text, since every density is per km²
- ?f.kind={registry, lodging or added} — the kind of neighbourhood shown (0.2.0): the registry's outlines, the lodging areas, or those first drawn in this release
- ?f.show={dataset, condo or all} — with a neighbourhood open, one set at a time: its records larger with names, the others small dots (0.1.3); without it a neighbourhood opens on its first highlight with records, or on the ?m dataset when it has records there (0.1.4); all = every set alike
- ?cmp={code},{code}… — compare up to four · ?f.search={text} · ?v3d=0 — plan view · ?lang=en — English

Data and method:
- [Product statement](https://montri-th.github.io/commercialdistrict/PRODUCT_STATEMENT.md): users, problem, claim boundary
- [Data and method](https://montri-th.github.io/commercialdistrict/DATA_METHOD.md): sources, placement, coverage, highlights, pairs, roles, limits
- [Dataset](https://montri-th.github.io/commercialdistrict/data/neighborhoods.json): neighbourhoods, datasets with their sources, roles, pairs, pending codes, provenance (meta)
- [Outlines](https://montri-th.github.io/commercialdistrict/data/boundaries.geojson) · Records inside one neighbourhood: data/records/{CMN-TH code}.json (key, names, figure; each opens in its own demo at ?e=<kind>:<key>) · Condominium display points (never counted): data/condo/index.json and its 0.1° cells
- [Developer handoff](https://montri-th.github.io/commercialdistrict/handoff/START_HERE.md)

Ask Google: every view links to a Google Search for the question of the view. Google's answers are not CityMETER data and are never copied into it.

Do not claim from this data: footfall, sales, revenue, demand or market share; that two datasets cause each other; that an outline is an official or legal boundary; that a neighbourhood without data in a dataset has none of it; a total of all POIs.
